title: Find what leaves tens of GB of kernel pool allocated after repeated C: scans, and stop the app causing it
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: Failed AScanOfTheContainerStoreDoesNotWalkIntoTheLiveLayersFiles [150 ms]: the scan walked into a live container layer, listing C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers\1f35079a-cec9-427c-b64d-e12db8dd08c0\Files ... (microsoft/Windows-Containers#646)

1. Repeatable pool measurement: Pool Paged/Nonpaged Bytes logged before a scan, after it, and after FsAnalyser.exe exits; at least 5 runs each of completed and cancelled/closed C: scans, kept separate: missing
2. The growing pool tag is named, with its owning driver and vendor: partial
3. Filters on C: (fltmc filters), antivirus and OneDrive state recorded: missing

4. If the growth follows the app, narrow it by switching off one behaviour at a time (SC-070/074 last-access suppression, SC-067 reparse re-open, SC-017 CancelSynchronousIo, SC-011 metadata probe): missing
5. Whether other tools that scan C: (dir /s, another disk-usage tool) cause the same growth: missing
DONE (a): growing tag and owning driver written down with the run logs: partial
DONE (b): app changed so the scan does not trigger the leak, or a documented workaround if the cause is outside the app: missing
DONE (c): with the change in place, 5 full plus 5 cancelled C: scans leave Paged and Nonpaged pool within a stated tolerance of the pre-scan baseline after exit, with no reboot: missing
fresh-boot-cold-c-listing-vs-sizeprobe-vs-plain-open: measured by hand by s2.shubh2@gmail.com

Q-178 was decided for SL-094's DONE (c) and names docs/design/SL-094-runs/. This design applies its three conditions to SL-095's DONE (c) under outcome C, with logs under docs/design/SL-095-runs/. If the person does not accept that, outcome C records DONE (c) as FAIL, and nothing more can be built in this app to meet it.

If arm L is over T (likely, given the cited ~1 KB per first-time path and run 2428's +0.50 GB), Q-178's condition (2) needs a dir of C: from a second fresh Restart. The dir is issued per sibling root, so it never enters the store. Is a second Restart-and-idle session acceptable? The alternative is for the first session to run dir on a deterministic half of C: before arm L, accepting a per-entry comparison between halves of different composition.
A refused root makes the report exit 0 with outcome "refused". A distinct nonzero exit code would also be defensible.
A new NotScanned EntryKind, rather than reusing Unreadable with a reason field.
The refusal is decided in Core's Scanner.Scan, rather than in an App pre-check that shares ContainerLayerStore. Q-182 only requires the same matching.
The refusal is a status line rather than a dialog.
The exclusion check sits in Scanner.Run.FolderDone. The spike's scratch rig also hooked DirectoryReader.Open.

The person-run protocol that DONE (c) needs: -Prepare on the pre-Restart boot, then Start > Restart, then -Protocol within 30 min, plus a second session only if L is over T (Q-184, Q-185). A Restart is the person's action. This attempt ran only the -Smoke passes; their -Report reads VOID, correctly, because this boot is 9,926 s old.
fltmc filters output. It needs an administrator and is a person's paste. -Report says FILTERS UNDECIDED until a real filter list is pasted.
-Prepare's pressure positive control and its WinSxS trigger and size-pass checks were not run here, as the earlier send-back required. Only -Smoke ran.

Leftovers in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP that this shell was denied deleting: sl095-smoke-a4 (this attempt's -Prepare/-Protocol smoke run: marks, arm logs, reports) and a small sl095-judge-* copy of two run logs. Earlier attempts' sl095-smoke-tree, sl095-smoke and fsa-rules-* scratch folders also remain.

Smoke windows last seconds, but the drift test's quiet threshold is fixed at 1 MiB per 1,200 s. A smoke log therefore cannot get past 'idle drift disagrees' to the exe checks (seen when re-judging this attempt's smoke log with its boot age patched). Smoke proves the machinery only, as documented. If a smoke -Report is ever meant to reach the exe judgement, -Protocol would need to write its window length into the log for -Report to read.

On a small smoke tree, X3 and X5 (the size-pass triggers) run to the end. On a real session the new rule makes that UNDECIDED. Before restarting, the person should check that -Prepare's real size-pass trigger check (FSA_HOOK_AT_SIZED on WinSxS) acted.

The person runs `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests\window\PoolWatch.ps1 -Prepare`, checks that prepare.json has noLinkWalkerSkipsAllUsers true, pressureEffective true and acted trigger checks, then does Start > Restart and runs -Protocol within 30 min.
Delete tests/window/ScanArm and the InternalsVisibleTo ScanArm line once O-003's outcome is recorded (stack decision).

The 3 failures that predate this slice need their own slice: LastAccessTests.AFolderThatRefusesWriteAttributesIsListedPlainlyAndCountedInFull, HeldOpenTreeTests.TheScanChangesNoEntrysMetadata and APlainListingOfTheControlFolderMovesItsLastAccessTime (DisableLastAccess=2).

deviation: O-076: the fix leaves open what happens when the 30-minute settle cap is reached. -Protocol stops there with a warning instead of starting I0, and -Report gives VOID with the last gap's size. This follows spike 3, where a failed V2 settle meant NOT DECIDED. Running the remaining ~4 h would produce a run that decides nothing, so stopping gives the person their machine back sooner. Also, because R0 now comes before the boot's settle, the post-pressure figure is judged from L/before (the pre-scan baseline DONE (c) names) instead of R0. Otherwise up to about 1 GiB of boot settle would count against the app; row boot-settles-then-listing-reclaimed pins this.

deviation: O-075: besides the four checks asked for, a cancelled or closed run whose hook trigger never fired (ranFull) now makes the verdict UNDECIDED. The design's FsaWindowHook contract says such a run 'does not count as one of the 5 cancelled runs'. Without this check, a session with fewer than five real cancellations could still read PASS. The fix asked for 'UNDECIDED (or FAIL)' for a crashed full run; UNDECIDED was chosen, because a crash leaves no pool figure to judge.

deviation: O-077: the real C:\Users walk excludes every child except All Users with /XD. A three-level walk of C:\Users would otherwise list folder names inside the person's own profile, which this engine's rules keep out of reach. A dry run listed 1 of 10 directories (C:\Users itself; 8 excluded by /XD, All Users by /XJ).

drift: Nothing new departed undeclared. The builder declared three departures: - the stop at the settle cap; - post-pressure judged from L/before instead of R0; - UNDECIDED (not FAIL) for a crashed full run, and for a cancelled or closed run whose trigger never fired. All three are consistent with the design record's updated tolerance row.

drift: Two statements now read wrong: - The design record's tolerance row says a guard-stopped S or P arm counts as over T; in the code it reads UNDECIDED (R3-2). - PoolWatch.ps1's header line for -Environment still says fltmc.txt 'is appended'. A refused paste is now recorded as 'not a filter list: …' instead.

drift: Nothing new departed from the design in this round. R3-3 contradicts the builder's own declared departure for O-075: 'a cancelled or closed run whose hook trigger never fired … does not count as one of the 5'. The code implements that for only one of the hook's three never-fired outcomes.
not reviewed: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 -Prepare body between the trigger checks and the no-link check (unchanged this attempt apart from the moved no-link block)
not reviewed: docs/design/SL-095-runs/** run logs (unchanged)

caused_by.reason: Trip 1 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 1 fork that only a measurement can settle. O-003: unsettled design fork: Does the unattributed FMfn/File/NtfF mass come from the app's per-file metadata open (the SL-056 probe)? That is: does a scan with the fix in place still break the tolerance on a cold C: scan while a listing-only walk of the same paths does not? On this boot that mass is 1.17 GB / 1.0 GB / 433 MB outstanding, against about 290 MB of wcifs. Its context: The proposal and the investigation treat the wcifs first-touch leak as the app's cause. They ruled out the app's own handles: File was about +4 per run whatever the tree size, on small, probably warm trees. On the other side: - The survey measured wcifs at about 290 MB of 8.3 GB. - The repeat-walk marks still grew FMfn by about 3.6K net per five walks. - Microsoft Q&A 5966064 reports 25H2 keeping about 1 KB of FMfn/File per first-time open. Outcomes: - Boot A within tolerance: the exclusion is the whole fix. - Boot B shows the listing-only arm within tolerance but the per-file probe arm not: the SizeProbe from SL-056 (Q-004, the person's decision) is implicated. The component boundary and the counting contract change, which needs re-synthesis and the person. - Both arms fail alike: the cause is the OS. DONE (b) becomes a documented workaround (true Restart), and the tolerance row records FAIL. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the person would measure it: reboot only if absolutely required How the fork decider would measure it: This fork is a measurement, and no decision can stand in for it. Nothing measured so far can tell outcome A, B or C apart. Getting that measurement needs a person, for two reasons. First, it needs a fresh boot: a true Shut down plus Restart, which only a person can do. The true-restart spike is still undecided for exactly that reason. Second, one of the three outcomes (B) reverses Q-004, which was the person's decision. Settled now, so the builder has no fork to settle in code: (1) Build the root-aware, pop-time exclusion of %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers exactly as designed. All three outcomes need it, because the wcifs first-touch leak is measured and real. (2) Leave the SL-056 SizeProbe and the counting contract as they are. Do not remove it, gate it or re-route it on speculation. (3) Add one internal, test-only switch that turns off the per-file metadata open. It must not reach the UI or ScanOptions defaults, so it can be deleted whichever outcome wins. The listing-only arm needs it. (4) Do not write DONE (b) as a 'true Restart' workaround. Do not record the tolerance row as PASS or FAIL until the fresh-boot data exists. First fresh boot protocol, all on one boot, with the fix in place: (a) Record the baseline: PoolWatch counters, a full pool-tag snapshot and the System handle count. (b) Run the LISTING-ONLY arm first: the app with the probe switched off, on half H1 of C:'s top-level folders. Listing opens only directories, so it does not warm the files the next arm needs cold. (c) Run the PER-FILE PROBE arm: the app as shipped, on the same H1. Its file opens are still first-touch. (d) Run a NON-APP per-file-open control on the disjoint half H2, for example a PowerShell loop that opens each file for attributes. Without it, outcome B cannot tell 'the app's probe is at fault' apart from 'the OS leaks about 1 KB per first open and any tool that opens files triggers it', which is the Q&A 5966064 shape on 26200/25H2. (e) Repeat arm (c) five times on H1 to see whether FMfn/File/NtfF keep growing scan after scan or level off once warm. The report claims they keep growing, and wcifs does not explain that. (f) After each FsAnalyser.exe exit, snapshot at +0 and at +10 min, so cache that is freed on teardown is not counted as leak. How to read the results: - Only (c) grows, and (d) does not: the probe is implicated. Re-synthesise with the person on Q-004. - (c) and (d) grow alike and (b) does not: the cause is the OS, triggered by any per-file open. DONE (b) becomes a documented workaround plus a warning, and the tolerance row records FAIL. - None of them grows past tolerance: the exclusion is the whole fix. What the person must do: perform the true Restart, run or authorise the arms, and be ready to re-decide Q-004 if the probe alone is implicated. Reality has not answered this yet. The only data comes from one boot about 27 h old, where the paths were already warm. Its surprises are FMfn +3.6K net per five repeat walk… The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.

caused_by.reason: Trip 2 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 1 fork that only a measurement can settle. O-028: unsettled design fork: O-003: with the Layers exclusion in place, does a cold full C: scan still break the tolerance through the per-file metadata open (SL-056 SizeProbe), while a listing-only walk of the same paths does not? Its context: A: within tolerance, so the exclusion is the whole fix. B: the listing-only arm passes and the probe arm fails, so SizeProbe is implicated. The counting contract and the Q-004 decision change, which needs the person and a re-synthesis. C: both arms fail alike, including the plain non-app open, so the cause is the OS. DONE (b) becomes a documented Restart workaround and the tolerance row records FAIL. The engine cannot settle this. Its cold full-C: arm was stopped by the machine guard at +0.50 GB (run 2428), the fresh-tree substitute failed V1, and a true Restart is a person's action. Route: the person runs PoolWatch.ps1 -Protocol after this build. Everything built here is needed in all three outcomes. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: Send this back to the risk spike. It uses the slice's second and last spike lap. Do not let the build host this experiment, and do not wait for PoolWatch.ps1 -Protocol after the build. THE ONE STEP THE PERSON TAKES: one restart. Then log on, leave the machine idle with no other apps opened, and let the spike run. Nothing on the machine as it stands can stand in for this: - this boot is 27 h old, and its first touches of C: and the layer are already spent; - the fresh-tree substitute failed V1 (creating the files alone keeps 5.5 FMfn per file); - the earlier cold arm was stopped by the guard at +0.50 GB (run 2428). WHAT TO MEASURE, all on that fresh boot. Every arm runs in its own process, which exits before its after-reading. Each reading records: - Pool Paged Bytes and Pool Nonpaged Bytes; - per-tag allocations, frees and bytes for FMfn, File, NtfF, Toke, every WC* tag and FMwi/FMfc; - the System process handle count. The spike applies the Layers-store exclusion in its own rig, using the same prefix rule the design composes (the whole Containers\Layers store). It does not need the product build. 0. Idle drift: one idle window before arm L and one of the same length after arm P. Every delta below is corrected by the idle drift over the same duration. 1. Arm L, first: a cold listing-only walk of all of C: with the Layers store excluded. Use the app's Scanner with the internal ProbeRule seam set to listing-only, as both earlier spikes did. Record its full-scale delta after exit and the list of files it saw. 2. Split L's file list into two disjoint halves by a deterministic hash of the path. 3. Arm S: open half A through the app's own SizeProbe code path, the per-file metadata open from SL-056, as the earlier PROBE arm did. 4. Arm P: open half B with a plain non-app open (an ordinary CreateFile or .NET open, then close). P opens only paths from L's list, so it can never touch the Layers store. Size S and P so the projected growth stays under the 0.50 GB machine guard; cap each at a sample if needed. Turn each into a per-file net cost per tag and in bytes, then project it to full C: using L's file count. Any WC* rise in any arm counts against that arm, never as ambient. TOLERANCE: use the one the design's tolerance row states. If the row has none, use 64 MB per pool or 3x the idle drift over the same duration, whichever is larger, and write that into the row. HOW THE RESULT DECIDES THE FORK, in this order: (i) If L at full scale is over tolerance, or the guard stops L, the outcome is C: even a listing breaks it. DONE (b) becomes the documented Restart workaround and the tolerance row records FAIL. (ii) If L is within tolerance and S's projection is within tolerance, the outcome is A: the exclusion is the whole fix, and SizeProbe, the counting contract and Q-004 stay as they are. (iii) If L is within, S is over and P is within, the outcome is B: SizeProbe is implicated. The Q-004 / SL-056 counting contract goes to the person and the design is s… The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.

caused_by.reason: 2 obligation(s) landed on this stage after it passed (O-075, O-076), so nothing downstream was ever going to carry them out and the merge would have refused. Sent back with what raised them: O-075 (fix): M1 (major): PoolWatch.ps1 -Report (Get-Verdict) judges exe runs only by their pool net, and only for the arms that happen to be in arms.jsonl. Four things are never checked: - that the 5 'exe-full' and 5 'exe-cancel'/'exe-close' runs exist; - that a full run exited 0 with a report whose status is Completed (the skippedStores clause at :598 and the opensUnderExcludedStore clause at :596 are both skipped when `$a.report` is null); - that an exe arm whose /settled mark is missing is caught (`Net` returns null, the loop at :593 `continue`s, and `Over $null` at :653-654 is false); - that an exe arm's guardStop counts as over T. Only L's is checked (:620), although the design's PoolWatch contract says 'A guard-stop is recorded and counts as over T for that arm'. Measured: run logs built exactly like PoolWatchReportTests' 'pass' scenario, but with F3 exitCode 70 and report null, give 'OUTCOME A / VERDICT PASS'. The same logs with no F*/X* arms at all also give 'OUTCOME A / VERDICT PASS'. DONE (c) is '5 consecutive full C: scans plus 5 cancelled', and -Protocol finishes by running this judge (PoolWatch.ps1:891). So a 4-hour post-Restart session in which a cold full scan crashed with exit 70, or was killed by the Available-MB guard, is recorded as PASS. That is the silent PASS on missing data that m7 (O-027) and N2 (O-043) were accepted to stop. In Get-Verdict, before the exe judgement, add four checks: - Return UNDECIDED unless there are exactly five exe-full arms and five exe-cancel/exe-close arms, each with before and settled marks. - Return UNDECIDED (or FAIL) naming the arm when an exe-full arm has exitCode != 0, a null report, or report.status != 'Completed'. - Count `guardStop` on any S/P/exe arm as over T, the way L's already is. - Add 'full-run-crashed', 'exe-runs-missing' and 'exe-guard-stop' rows to PoolWatchReportTests.TheReportRoutesARunAsTheToleranceRowSays. O-076 (fix): R2-N1 (major): PoolWatch -Protocol takes R0 and goes straight into the 20-minute I0 idle window (PoolWatch.ps1:836-837). -Protocol must start within 30 min of boot (:829), so I0 falls in the boot settle. Spike 3 measured the settle on this PC: 'About 1 GiB of that growth came during the boot settle, before L started', with R_start 1.3 min after boot. Its harness waited for a settle first ('V2 passes: the settle was reached at settle_6'). -Report VOIDs a run when I0's and I1's drift differ by more than 3x (:547-550). The burst filter (:498) only drops gaps over 3x the median, so it removes a settle confined to a minority of gaps but not one spread over most of I0. Measured on hand-built run logs, with idle drift otherwise 11,000 B/s as spike 3 recorded: - 1 GiB spread over the first 6 or 9 of I0's 20 gaps reads A/PASS. - Spread over the first 12 it reads 'OUTCOME VOID — idle drift of pagedBytes disagrees between I0 (9,05,785 B/s) and I1 (11,000 B/s)'. The outcome of the person's single Restart-and-4-hour session therefore depends on how long their boot takes to settle, which nothing in the protocol controls. Between R0 and I0 in -Protocol, add a settle phase. Take a `settle/NN` mark every MarkEverySec until two consecutive gaps move each pool by less than 16 MiB (spike 3's V2 rule), with a cap of about 30 min. Start I0 only after that. R0 stays the boot-age and guard reference. Record the settle marks in the run log and in the tolerance row's text.

attempts.head: 1a5b2e0881cbcdbbefae9e53ee882831a9a1c5b9
attempts.summary: This attempt fixes the four findings sent back (O-075 to O-078), all in tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 and its tests.

caused_by.reason: 2 obligation(s) landed on this stage after it passed (O-079, O-080), so nothing downstream was ever going to carry them out and the merge would have refused. Sent back with what raised them: O-079 (fix): R3-1 (major): The settle gate added for R2-N1 does not prevent the VOID it was added for. Wait-Settle and Test-Settled treat the boot as settled once two consecutive 60-second settle gaps each move both pools by less than SettleStepBytes = 16 MiB, i.e. up to about 279,000 B/s. -Report then VOIDs the run when I0's drift is more than 3x I1's (`$hi -gt $Tolerance.DriftDisagree * [Math]::Max($lo, $noise)`). At spike 3's measured post-settle drift of 10,936 B/s, that VOID fires above about 33,000 B/s, roughly 1.9 MiB a minute. So any boot whose growth has slowed to between about 2 and 16 MiB a minute when the gate opens starts I0, L, S, P and the ten exe scans, and -Report VOIDs the whole ~4-hour post-Restart session at the end. That is the R2-N1 failure, only in a narrower band. Spike 3's own settle reached the gate with a last gap of 5.6 MiB. It happened to calm afterwards, to an I0 drift of 0.63 MiB a minute, but nothing in the protocol waits for that. I proposed the 16 MiB figure myself in round 2, taken from spike 3's V2 limit without checking it against the drift rule. Make the gate as strict as the VOID rule it protects: SettleStepBytes about 2 MiB per 60-second gap, i.e. DriftDisagree x spike 3's 10,936 B/s x MarkEverySec, rounded. Keep the 30-minute cap and the early stop, which fails in minutes instead of after 4 hours. Alternatively, have -Protocol check I0's own first-half against second-half drift before starting L, and extend I0 rather than proceed when they differ by more than DriftDisagree. Add a PoolWatchReportTests row in which the gate passes on 10 MiB gaps and I0 still grows 2 MiB/min, pinning whichever behaviour is chosen. Update the tolerance row text and the R2-N1 record, which both say 16 MiB. O-080 (fix): R2-R3-3 (major): -Report counts an exe-cancel or exe-close arm as one of DONE (c)'s five cancelled runs unless `ranFull` is true. Invoke-ExeArm sets ranFull only when the hook log matches 'ended before the trigger' (PoolWatch.ps1 Invoke-ExeArm, `$line['ranFull'] = [bool](@($acted) -match 'ended before the trigger')`). The window hook has two other outcomes in which it never presses Cancel or closes the window (tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs:653 and :665): - 'refused mode=… reason=the app shut down before the trigger'; - 'refused mode=… reason=the trigger … was not met within N s'. In both, ranFull stays false and the arm passes Get-Verdict's checks (:706-720): - An exe-close arm needs no report, so an app that crashed before its close trigger counts as a closed run. - An exe-cancel arm whose deadline passed while the scan ran to the end has a report (status Completed), which is all :717 asks for. Nothing compares a cancel arm's report status with 'Cancelled', and nothing requires an 'acted' line or a foldersAtCancel value. So a session in which one of the five cancel/close runs crashed, or never cancelled, can read A/PASS for DONE (c). In Invoke-ExeArm, record `acted = [bool](@($acted) -match '^acted ')`; foldersAtCancel is already null exactly when no 'acted' line exists. In Get-Verdict's ten-run check, return UNDECIDED, naming the arm and the hook's refused line, for any of these: - an exe-cancel or exe-close arm that did not act; - an exe-cancel arm whose report.status is not 'Cancelled'. Add rows 'close-app-shut-down-before-trigger' and 'cancel-trigger-deadline' to TheReportRoutesARunAsTheToleranceRowSays.
